item.title: She went to college to become a social worker. Now she's joined the skilled trades
item.description: While the rise of AI continues to fuel the debate over whether college is worth the cost, apprenticeships in the skilled trades are having a moment, drawing in people of all backgrounds including college graduates.
item.content:encoded:

item.title: Do school cellphone bans work? New study says yes – but it's complicated
item.description: A new study of school cellphone bans finds they may help students make up for some of the learning they've lost since 2013 – a divergence from earlier study results.
item.content:encoded:

item.title: More people are getting the flu. Should you get a flu shot before you travel?
item.description: Thanksgiving is just around the corner, just as millions of Americans are expected to travel for the holidays. Another thing that's upon us? Cold and flu season.

item.title: Russia downs over 1,400 Ukrainian drones as Kyiv hits a key bridge in Crimea
item.description: Ukraine's forces targeted a key rail and road bridge between Russia and the Crimean Peninsula for a second day. Moscow's forces, meanwhile, fired ballistic missiles and drones at Kyiv.
item.content:encoded:

item.title: California sues OpenAI over hacking risks
item.description: The state's attorney general started investigating OpenAI after the Hugging Face attack and now says this attack was "entirely foreseeable" due to OpenAI's poor security practices.
item.content:encoded:

item.title: U.S. tightens controls on remote access to AI technology amid Nvidia fallout
item.description: The new rule closes a loophole that existed that allowed Chinese companies to still access advanced AI chips remotely, despite U.S. restrictions on their physical sale to China.
item.content:encoded:

item.title: U.N. talks seek to rein in 'killer robots' as fears over AI weapons grow
item.description: Countries are meeting in Geneva to negotiate rules on weapons that can select and kill targets without human intervention. But with the U.S., Russia and Israel resisting legally binding controls, campaigners fear the window to act is closing.
item.content:encoded:

item.title: Nearly two million people are behind bars in the US. How did we get here?
item.description:
Lynn Novick's new, four-part PBS documentary series, Crime and Punishment in America, goes inside the U.S. prison system and explores how
our approach to criminals has changed over time.
